# Let's parse the content of the file to extract the list of song titles and artists.
# The format is "- <Song Title> by <Artist(s)>", possibly with multiple artists separated by commas.

import re

file_content = old_songs_file["content"]
# Extract lines that start with "- "
song_lines = [line.strip()[2:] for line in file_content.splitlines() if line.strip().startswith("- ")]
# Parse each line into (title, [artists])
old_songs = []
for line in song_lines:
    match = re.match(r"(.+?) by (.+)", line)
    if match:
        title = match.group(1).strip()
        artists = [artist.strip() for artist in match.group(2).split(",")]
        old_songs.append({"title": title, "artists": artists})
print(old_songs)

steps.code:
# Now, let's match each song in the playlists to the old_songs list.
# We'll consider a match if both the title and at least one artist name match (case-insensitive).
# We'll build a mapping of playlist_id -> list of song_ids to remove, and also collect all matched song_ids for the new playlist.

matched_songs_by_playlist = {}
archived_song_ids = set()

for playlist in all_playlists:
    playlist_id = playlist["playlist_id"]
    matched_songs = []
    for song_id in playlist["song_ids"]:
        song = song_metadata[str(song_id)]
        song_title = song["title"].strip().lower()
        song_artists = set(artist["name"].strip().lower() for artist in song["artists"])
        for old_song in old_songs:
            old_title = old_song["title"].strip().lower()
            old_artists = set(a.strip().lower() for a in old_song["artists"])
            if song_title == old_title and (song_artists & old_artists):
                matched_songs.append(song_id)
                archived_song_ids.add(song_id)
                break
